code='''def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Identify repeated-color palette strip; its nonzero colors specify copies.
    coords=[(r,c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c] != 0]
    bycolor={}
    for r,c in coords: bycolor.setdefault(grid[r][c], []).append((r,c))
    # Main motif is the color with the largest connected shape; palette colors are in a straight repeated strip.
    # Locate the compact repeated line object (same cells across rows or a single row).
    lines=[]
    for r in range(h):
        vals=[grid[r][c] for c in range(w) if grid[r][c]]
        if len(vals)>=2: lines.append(vals)
    for c in range(w):
        vals=[grid[r][c] for r in range(h) if grid[r][c]]
        if len(vals)>=2: lines.append(vals)
    palette=max(lines,key=len)
    colors=palette
    # motif = connected component not belonging to palette's repeated strip
    pcells=set()
    for r in range(h):
        vals=[grid[r][c] for c in range(w) if grid[r][c]]
        if vals==palette:
            pcells.update((r,c) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c])
    for c in range(w):
        vals=[grid[r][c] for r in range(h) if grid[r][c]]
        if vals==palette:
            pcells.update((r,c) for r in range(h) if grid[r][c])
    motif=[(r,c,grid[r][c]) for r,c in coords if (r,c) not in pcells]
    # retain only dominant motif color cells (exclude accidental palette overlaps)
    from collections import Counter
    cnt=Counter(v for r,c,v in motif)
    color=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    motif=[(r,c) for r,c,v in motif if v==color]
    r0=min(r for r,c in motif); r1=max(r for r,c in motif); c0=min(c for r,c in motif); c1=max(c for r,c in motif)
    height=r1-r0+1; width=c1-c0+1
    center=(r0+r1)//2
    out=[[0]*w for _ in range(h)]
    start=center-(len(colors)*height)//2
    for i,col in enumerate(colors):
        for r,c in motif:
            rr=start+i*height+(r-r0); cc=c
            if 0<=rr<h: out[rr][cc]=col
    return out
'''
